title: Delhi Deputy Mayor Dies After Monkey Attack
summary: New Delhi deputy mayor S.S. Bajwa was attacked by a group of rhesus macaques while reading on his terrace and fell to the ground below, suffering fatal head injuries. He died in intensive care the next day. The incident intensified debate over the city's large resident monkey population.

title: Illegal Pet Macaque Bites Bank Employee
summary: An owner brought his pet juvenile macaque into a North Side bank, where it bit a female employee. Animal Care Services located the owner off Babcock Road and seized the monkey; the animal lacked required permits.

title: Eight Macaques Escape University of Louisiana Lafayette
summary: Eight macaques escaped a University of Louisiana-Lafayette research facility. Referenced in later Alpha Genesis coverage as an earlier comparable lab-escape incident; independent confirmation is thinner than for the SC cases.

title: Capuchin 'Carter' Attacks Hospital Worker, Escapes Into Woods
summary: A pet capuchin monkey named Carter scratched and attacked a maintenance worker who tried to contain him in a bin at Carolinas Medical Center-University, then fled into a wooded area. He was recaptured the next day.

title: UW-Madison Primate Lab Escape Causes Amputation Injury
summary: During a cage-cleaning procedure at the Wisconsin National Primate Research Center, a monkey escaped its enclosure and engaged a caged primate, causing trauma that required amputation of a digit. USDA inspection records document similar escape incidents at the facility around this period.

title: Feral Rhesus Macaque Colony at Silver Springs Confirmed Carrying Herpes B
summary: A CDC field study sampled Silver Springs State Park's roughly 175 free-ranging rhesus macaques and found 4%-14% actively shedding herpes B virus, which is often fatal in humans if untreated. Date is an estimate based on the study's fall 2015 sampling window.

title: 19 Monkeys Escape Alpha Genesis, Recaptured Within Six Hours
summary: 19 monkeys escaped the Alpha Genesis Primate Research Center after a cage door failure. All 19 were recaptured within about six hours. Date is estimated from reporting that only specified 'a Sunday afternoon in 2016.'

title: Second Orangutan Escapes Enclosure at Busch Gardens Within Weeks
summary: A different orangutan got loose from its enclosure at Busch Gardens Tampa Bay and was at large for about an hour before being recaptured -- roughly two weeks before a second, separate orangutan escape at the same park (Luna Bella, July 2016).

title: Orangutan "Luna Bella" Escapes Enclosure at Busch Gardens
summary: An orangutan named Luna Bella got out of her habitat in the Jungala area of Busch Gardens Tampa Bay, prompting a partial park evacuation. A Florida Fish and Wildlife officer tranquilized her and she was returned to her enclosure without incident.

title: Rhesus Macaque Sighted 50 Miles South of Silver Springs Colony
summary: Florida Fish and Wildlife officers confirmed a rhesus macaque photographed by a resident in Apopka, roughly 50 miles south of the established Silver Springs feral colony, indicating the invasive population's range was expanding.

title: Hurricane Maria Threatens Cayo Santiago Rhesus Colony
summary: Hurricane Maria struck Cayo Santiago ('Monkey Island'), a Puerto Rico field station home to roughly 1,500 free-ranging rhesus macaques used in longstanding primate research. Most animals survived and were later studied for behavioral adaptation.

title: Transport Rhesus Macaque Escapes Crate at San Antonio Airport
summary: A rhesus macaque named Dawkins, being transported from Brown University to a sanctuary via air cargo, escaped his crate at San Antonio International Airport and led staff on a chase through the baggage claim area before being tranquilized about two hours later.

title: Pet Spider Monkey 'Spanky' Attacks Home Depot Employee
summary: A pet spider monkey named Spanky, left in a vehicle while its owner shopped, got loose and attacked a Home Depot employee, climbing on her back and biting and scratching her, before being subdued.

title: Teen Steals Ring-Tailed Lemur "Isaac" from Santa Ana Zoo
summary: A 19-year-old broke into the Santa Ana Zoo after hours, cut a hole in the lemur/capuchin enclosure with bolt cutters, and took Isaac, then North America's oldest captive ring-tailed lemur (32). Isaac was found unharmed in a container outside a Newport Beach hotel the next day; the thief pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 90 days in prison plus restitution.
sourceName: US Dept. of Justice / NBC News

title: Herpes-Carrying Silver Springs Monkey Population Reported Growing
summary: Researchers confirmed the invasive, herpes B-carrying rhesus macaque population around Silver Springs/Ocala National Forest was continuing to grow, with estimates of roughly 175-250+ animals and expanding range, renewing debate over management options.

title: Siamang Gibbon "Hantu" Escapes Enclosure at Baton Rouge Zoo
summary: Hantu, a 3-year-old siamang (a large gibbon species), got through a small hole in his enclosure mesh and climbed a nearby tree at the Baton Rouge Zoo. Response staff tranquilized and recaptured him within about five minutes; no one was hurt.

title: St. Petersburg Woman Bitten in Unprovoked Rhesus Macaque Attack
summary: A woman was bitten and scratched by a rhesus macaque while sitting on her porch in St. Petersburg, in the same Tampa Bay area long associated with the famous 'Mystery Monkey of Tampa Bay' feral escapee. Date is approximate based on available reporting.

title: USDA Fines UW-Madison $74,000 for Primate Welfare Violations
summary: USDA fined the University of Wisconsin-Madison $74,000 for 28 Animal Welfare Act violations, many involving monkeys, including deaths, injuries, and escapes documented at its primate research center since 2014.

title: Orangutan Bites Zookeeper's Arm at Erie Zoo
summary: A zookeeper sustained puncture and bite wounds to his forearm when bitten by an orangutan named Dasa at the Erie Zoo. The animal was contained in her exhibit throughout; the keeper was treated at a hospital for non-life-threatening injuries.

title: Ring-Tailed Lemur "Maki" Stolen from San Francisco Zoo
summary: Maki, a 21-year-old ring-tailed lemur, was taken from the San Francisco Zoo and found safe two days later at a church playground about four miles away. A San Rafael man was arrested and booked in connection with the theft.

title: Pet Pigtailed Macaque Escapes, Injures Four in Reno Neighborhood
summary: A permitted pet pigtailed macaque named Gebbe got loose in Reno's Somersett neighborhood and scratched and bit four bystanders before being captured and placed under a 10-day rabies quarantine.

title: Deputy Fatally Shoots Pet Chimpanzee 'Buck' After Attack on Owner's Daughter
summary: Buck, the last privately owned chimpanzee in Oregon, got loose from his cage and bit his owner's 50-year-old daughter multiple times. A responding Umatilla County sheriff's deputy shot and killed the chimp; both women were hospitalized.

title: Nonprofit Moves to Build Sanctuary for Decades-Old Dania Beach Vervet Colony
summary: Reporting detailed the ~80-year-old Dania Beach feral vervet monkey colony (descended from 1940s escapees of the Dania Chimpanzee Farm), noting the group had lost more than 10 members in a year to electrocution, vehicle strikes, and illegal capture, spurring a sanctuary-building effort.

title: Pet Capuchin Bites Trick-or-Treating Child at Halloween Event
summary: A pet capuchin monkey named Gia bit down on a child's hand and would not let go during a trick-or-treating haunted-house event, prompting a lawsuit against the owners.

title: Lab Monkey Transport Truck Crashes in Pennsylvania, Several Escape
summary: A truck carrying about 100 crab-eating macaques to a laboratory crashed with a dump truck near Danville, Pennsylvania. Four monkeys escaped the wreckage; three were euthanized and one was recovered, prompting a public search and safety warnings.

title: Colobus Monkey 'Raj' Briefly Escapes Louisville Zoo Exhibit
summary: A colobus monkey named Rajesh ('Raj') escaped his exhibit at the Louisville Zoo after a small transfer-chute panel failed. He was found a few feet outside the exhibit and returned safely about 90 minutes later. He was later transferred to Memphis Zoo, where he escaped again in 2024.

title: Wild Monkeys Injure Dozens in Yamaguchi Attack Spree
summary: A string of at least 42 monkey attacks injured residents, mostly children and the elderly, in the Japanese city of Yamaguchi over several weeks; animals entered homes through screen doors and windows. Officials formed a tranquilizer-gun unit and killed one matching macaque, but attacks continued, indicating multiple animals were involved.

title: Alpha Genesis Cited for 'Critical' Fence Failures After Six Escape Incidents
summary: A September 2022 USDA inspection cited Alpha Genesis with a 'critical' violation after six separate 2022 incidents in which at least 11 monkeys escaped their primary enclosures, though they stayed within the perimeter fence and were rounded up.

title: Capuchin 'Jack' Escapes Suncoast Primate Sanctuary, Spotted on Pinellas Trail
summary: A 30-year-old black-capped capuchin named Jack darted out of his enclosure at Suncoast Primate Sanctuary when a snagged net let him slip through the main door. He was filmed by a cyclist on the Pinellas Trail and recaptured the next morning.

title: Chimpanzee "Mara" Escapes Puerto Rico Zoo Over Holiday Period
summary: Mara, a 22-year-old female chimpanzee, opened a hole in the wire mesh of her enclosure at a Puerto Rico zoo during a low-staffing holiday period and was loose for several hours before being sedated and returned. Exact date is approximate -- sourcing did not pin down the specific day. The zoo was later shut down and its animals relocated in a broader 2023 rescue effort.

title: Two Emperor Tamarin Monkeys Stolen From Dallas Zoo
summary: Two emperor tamarin monkeys were deliberately cut out of their Dallas Zoo enclosure and stolen, found safe a day later at an abandoned home nearby. A suspect was arrested on animal cruelty charges and later indicted on felony burglary counts amid a wider string of zoo security incidents.

title: Macaque Flees Into Lion Enclosure After Losing Zoo Fight
summary: A female rhesus macaque at Wuxi Zoo lost a fight with another monkey, jumped an electric fence to flee, and wandered into the zoo's lion enclosure. Staff recaptured her and returned her to the monkey hill unharmed. Translated from Chinese-language local reporting.

title: Escaped Pet Monkey 'Jack' Attacks Neighbor
summary: A neighbor's pet monkey named Jack got loose, tried to break into Brittany Parker's home, then attacked her — nearly detaching her ear and requiring reconstructive plastic surgery. A family member shot and killed the monkey days later.

title: Baby Gibbon Briefly Escapes Enclosure at San Antonio Zoo
summary: A 3.5-month-old baby gibbon got outside its habitat at the San Antonio Zoo. It stayed close to its mother, who kept watch, and animal care specialists safely retrieved the infant within minutes.

title: Exotic Animal Dealer Surrenders Ring-Tailed Lemurs After Welfare Violations
summary: A Michigan exotic-animal dealer entered a federal consent decree surrendering nearly 150 animals, including multiple ring-tailed lemurs, after allegations he prematurely separated a baby lemur from its mother to sell for $3,500 and violated Animal Welfare Act housing/care standards. He is now permanently barred from dealing in AWA-regulated animals.

title: "Momo" At Large, Indianapolis IN
summary: A privately-owned capuchin nicknamed "Momo" spent roughly a day loose on Indianapolis's east side before being captured and surrendered to the Indianapolis Zoo. Owner later fined; animal ruled unfit to return home.

title: Silverback Gorilla "Elmo" Charges Keepers in Viral Fort Worth Zoo Video
summary: Video that went viral in 2024 (months after filming) shows two zookeepers sharing a space with a 34-year-old silverback gorilla, Elmo, who charged toward them during feeding time. No physical contact occurred and no one was injured, but the footage raised questions about keeper-safety protocols.

title: Ring-Tailed Lemur "Maki" Stolen from San Francisco Zoo a Second Time
summary: The same lemur, Maki, was again stolen from the Lipman Family Lemur Forest habitat at the San Francisco Zoo, missing for roughly two days before being found at a children's playground about five miles away. A suspect was arrested in connection with the theft. Exact date is approximate.

title: Colobus Monkey 'Mykel' Recaptured After Roughly Six Months Loose
summary: An Angolan colobus monkey named Mykel escaped Singapore Zoo and evaded capture for roughly half a year, reportedly after being pushed out by his troop. He was eventually caught in a net after falling from a tree, exhausted. dateStart is an estimate based on the reported ~6-month timeframe. Translated from Chinese-language reporting.

title: "Bradley" Escape, Walterboro SC
summary: A 15-year-old pet macaque named Bradley escaped from a residence. After several days searching, officials confirmed the animal was not recovered alive.

title: Chimpanzee "Mara" Escape, Indianapolis Zoo
summary: A chimpanzee named Mara briefly got past a barrier in the zoo's newly opened International Chimpanzee Complex. Contained on zoo grounds and returned to the exhibit same day.

title: Infant Monkey's Arm Amputated After Escape at Yerkes Primate Center
summary: A baby monkey under three months old escaped through a roughly 3-inch hole in its cage at Emory's Yerkes National Primate Research Center and broke its arm, which had to be surgically amputated above the elbow. USDA cited this as a critical repeat violation.

title: Orangutan "Kembali" Briefly Accesses Restricted Area at Toronto Zoo
summary: A male orangutan named Kembali got into an area just outside his habitat at the Toronto Zoo. Staff quickly cleared guests from the vicinity before safely returning him to his enclosure.

title: Maryland's Traveling Exotic Animal Act Ban (Covering Primates) Takes Effect
summary: Maryland's HB 379 took effect October 1, 2024, banning the use of nonhuman primates, big cats, bears, and elephants in traveling entertainment acts, with civil penalties up to $2,000 per violation, part of the state's broader statutory ban on private primate possession.

title: Colobus Monkey Escape, Memphis Zoo
summary: A male colobus monkey bent open his transport crate while being moved between zoo buildings. Stayed near his familiar exhibit and was recontained same day. Zoo grounds briefly secured. This was the same colobus monkey, 'Raj,' who had previously escaped his enclosure at Louisville Zoo in 2022 before being transferred to Memphis.

title: Bonobo Bite Leads to Partial Thumb Amputation for Cincinnati Zoo Worker
summary: During morning feeding and medication rounds, a bonobo bit through a protective mesh barrier and caught a primate care worker's thumb, resulting in partial amputation, at the Cincinnati Zoo. The bonobo remained contained throughout; no other staff, guests, or animals were involved.

title: MAJOR EVENT: Alpha Genesis Facility Breach
summary: 43 young rhesus macaques escaped a primate research facility after a caretaker failed to secure an enclosure door. Authorities urged nearby residents to keep doors and windows locked. Animals ranged through surrounding woodland for nearly three months, surviving a winter storm, before the final holdouts were lured back with peanut butter and jelly sandwiches.

title: Orange City Police Warn Residents of Wild Monkey Sightings
summary: Orange City Police received multiple resident reports of rhesus macaques roaming the city in mid-December 2024, part of a wider wave of 2024 macaque sightings across central Florida communities, prompting warnings not to feed the animals.

title: Baby Spider Monkey Found in Rolls-Royce During DUI Traffic Stop
summary: California Highway Patrol pulled over a speeding Rolls-Royce and found a one-month-old spider monkey wearing a onesie, malnourished and in critical condition, along with drugs and multiple cellphones. The driver was arrested for DUI and illegal possession of an exotic animal; the monkey was taken to Oakland Zoo for treatment.

title: Orangutan Bites Keeper Through Barrier at Woodland Park Zoo
summary: During a routine protected-contact training session at Woodland Park Zoo, an orangutan bit a zookeeper through a mesh barrier, causing a serious but non-life-threatening injury to the keeper's hand. The zoo said it would review its protective barrier protocols following the incident.

title: Four Orangutans Briefly Escape Enclosure at Denver Zoo
summary: A door connecting the orangutans' bedrooms to a secured, staff-only side hallway malfunctioned at the Denver Zoo, allowing four orangutans into the hallway. They never accessed public areas or the outdoors; staff safely returned all four to their habitat.

title: Men Indicted for Illegal Exotic Primate Photo-Shoot Business
summary: Baltimore County Police arrested two men after a paid photo shoot with a severely malnourished spider monkey and a ring-tailed lemur at a Towson Town Center parking garage. A follow-up undercover sting by Baltimore County Police, the FBI, and federal wildlife officials led to a search warrant at a Middle River apartment, where the malnourished lemur, an infant spider monkey, and other exotic animals were seized. The men face 23 felony and misdemeanor counts including animal cruelty; the animals are now in the Maryland Zoo's care.

title: Capuchin Monkey Escapes Zootastic Park, Later Struck by Car
summary: A 5-year-old female capuchin monkey pulled apart wire cage bars and escaped Zootastic Park in Troutman, NC, and was filmed climbing utility lines. About a week later she was struck by a vehicle in the area; she survived and was returned to her owner.

title: MAJOR EVENT: I-59 Transport Crash
summary: A truck hauling 21 rhesus macaques from a Tulane University-linked research shipment overturned on Interstate 59, spilling crates labeled "live monkeys" into roadside grass. Several animals were killed in the crash or during the search; the last free-ranging holdouts were recovered days later. Owner and exact research purpose were not immediately disclosed, fueling public speculation. One survivor, nicknamed 'Forrest,' was later rehomed at a New Jersey sanctuary; separately, a local resident shot and killed one of the loose monkeys near their home, citing fear for their children's safety.

title: Chimpanzee Escapes Exhibit at Indianapolis Zoo, Triggers Lockdown
summary: A female chimpanzee got outside the International Chimpanzee Complex enclosure at the Indianapolis Zoo, prompting a roughly two-hour emergency lockdown with guests moved to secure locations. Fire department responded; the chimp was sedated and returned safely with no injuries reported.

title: Monkey Escapes Concepción Zoo, Captured During Street Patrol
summary: A monkey escaped the municipal zoo in Concepción, Chile, and was filmed by neighbors walking along a local road, nearly struck by a car at one point. Municipal officials captured the animal during a patrol conducted for an unrelated heatwave response. Translated from Spanish-language local reporting.

title: Troop of Barbary Macaques Maul Tourist on the Rock
summary: A troop of Barbary macaques attacked a 70-year-old visitor on Gibraltar's Upper Rock, leaving her with serious injuries, lasting nerve pain, and psychological trauma. Gibraltar's famous free-ranging macaque population is a major tourist draw but has a history of occasional aggressive encounters. Date is approximate based on available reporting.

title: Bonobo Cracks Safety Glass Charging at Visitors, Closing Memphis Zoo Exhibit
summary: A bonobo launched itself at an interior viewing pane in the Primate Canyon exhibit at Memphis Zoo, cracking the specially fabricated safety glass. No visitors or the animal were injured, but the exhibit closed for an extended repair due to the custom glass needed.

title: 'Monkey Whisperer' Sentenced to Federal Prison for Repeat Primate Trafficking
summary: Jimmy Wayne Hammonds ('the Monkey Whisperer'), already a convicted Lacey Act primate trafficker, was sentenced to nine months in federal prison and a $60,000 fine after selling marmosets and other primates to an undercover US Fish & Wildlife agent while on probation for the same crime. The 67 animals he was forced to surrender included ring-tailed lemurs alongside the capuchins and other monkeys that were the operation's primary focus.

title: Injured Spider Monkey Illegally Kept as Pet Seized in Grand Island
summary: New York DEC seized an illegally kept pet spider monkey from a Grand Island home after a tip; the owner surrendered the animal, which was found to have a broken wrist and rickets from poor diet and care. It was transferred to a licensed primate sanctuary.

title: US Fish & Wildlife Details Effort Dismantling Florida Monkey Trafficking Ring
summary: US Fish & Wildlife Service published an official account of its multi-year undercover investigation dismantling an illegal Florida primate-trafficking network, tied to the 'Monkey Whisperer' prosecutions, detailing methods used to sell protected primates via encrypted messaging and false documentation.

title: Nearly 100 Monkeys Escape Enclosure, Invade Lopburi Neighborhoods
summary: Nearly 100 long-tailed macaques broke out of a damaged municipal enclosure in Lopburi, Thailand, invading homes and a police station before staff prevented over 1,000 additional monkeys from joining the escape. Officials recaptured 99 using tranquilizer darts and baited cages, and reinforced the enclosure with a double-layer design.

title: PETA Seeks USDA Investigation Into Two New UW-Madison Monkey Injury Incidents
summary: PETA asked USDA to investigate two 2026 incidents at UW-Madison's primate research facility: one rhesus macaque was attacked through an adjacent food-access opening and required an arm amputation; in a second, unsecured interlocking cage doors let neighboring macaques fight, leaving one with severe oral injuries. PETA says USDA has cited UW-Madison for eight Animal Welfare Act violations since 2024.

title: USDA Cites Lab-Monkey Supplier Inotiv for Amputation Injuries at Texas Facility
summary: USDA issued a critical Animal Welfare Act citation against Inotiv's LAMS West Inc. laboratory-monkey supply facility in Alice, Texas, after a pattern of injuries: an infant crab-eating macaque's arm was amputated after being crushed by a cage door, and other macaques suffered leg and toe amputations from poorly designed enclosures through 2025 and into a January 2026 incident. The citation was publicized as parent company Inotiv was in Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. No escape occurred; the animals remained contained at the facility throughout.

title: Trafficker Arrested in Salvador, Brazil, for Illegal Capuchin Monkey Sales
summary: Civil Police in Salvador, Bahia, rescued two capuchin monkeys from homes in the Liberdade and Uruguai neighborhoods and arrested a 35-year-old man accused of selling at least three capuchins for between R$15,000 and R$20,000 each using forged paperwork. Brazil's environmental agency IBAMA fined him more than R$200,000, and investigators believe a larger supplier network is involved. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting.

title: Free-Roaming Monkey Bites Child in Monte Alegre, Brazil, Evades Capture
summary: A monkey that had been living freely in the Curaxi neighborhood of Monte Alegre, Para, entered a home and bit a child who was watching television, causing bleeding leg wounds. Residents said they had previously reported the animal to local authorities. Civil Defense and the municipal environmental agency attempted to capture it but the monkey evaded them and remains at large. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting.

title: Mexican Wildlife Agency Seizes Spider Monkey Kept as Pet Inside a Church
summary: Mexico's federal environmental enforcement agency, Profepa, seized a spider monkey that had been kept as a pet inside a house-turned-church in Manzanillo, Colima, following a citizen report. The animal, an endangered species under Mexican law, appeared physically healthy but showed signs of human imprinting, complicating chances of eventual wild release, and was transferred to a licensed wildlife management unit. It was the second spider-monkey seizure in Colima state within a month. Translated from Spanish-language reporting.

title: Long-Tailed Macaque Injures Nearly 20 Residents Over Two-Week Span in Sumatra
summary: A single long-tailed macaque with a facial scar bit and scratched at least 18 to 19 residents of Tembilahan, Riau province, Indonesia, over roughly two weeks, mostly targeting people who were alone or off guard, and panic reportedly closed dozens of local schools. Conservation officers (BBKSDA Riau) trapped the animal on August 6 and placed it under 14-day observation; rapid testing for zoonotic disease came back negative. Officials suspect the macaque had previously been abused by humans. Translated from Indonesian-language reporting.

title: Tibetan Macaque Bites Tourist at Sichuan Scenic Area
summary: A wild Tibetan macaque bit a female tourist at the Dafeishui scenic area on Xiling Snow Mountain, within Giant Panda National Park in Dayi County, Sichuan, China. Park staff disinfected the wound on site, issued documentation for medical reimbursement, and arranged priority hospital treatment; staff noted bites are far less common than scratches at the site. Translated from Chinese-language reporting.

title: Wild Monkeys Repeatedly Enter Da Nang Residential Area, Attack People and Pets
summary: One or two wild monkeys have repeatedly entered residential areas of Da Nang, Vietnam, over more than a month, climbing onto rooftops, searching for food, and attacking residents and pets when provoked. Late-August reporting says Son Tra Peninsula macaques have grown bolder, moving further into city streets to snatch food from tourists. Forest rangers captured a rhesus macaque blamed for repeated incursions on Dao Duy Ky, Bui Lam, and Hoang Quoc Viet streets in Nai Hien Dong ward on September 8 and released it back into the Son Tra mountain habitat. Translated from Vietnamese-language reporting.

title: Recurring Monkey Troop Attacks Injure Multiple Residents in Pilibhit, India
summary: A troop of monkeys caused repeated trouble across several neighborhoods of Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh, India, in early-to-mid August 2026, injuring an elderly woman and a girl in one incident and continuing to disrupt the Sahukara, Than Singh, Kesari Singh, and Ekta Nagar areas despite official efforts to manage the population. Troop size is an approximate estimate. Translated from Hindi-language reporting.

title: Langur Smuggling Racket Busted in Budaun, India
summary: Police in Budaun, Uttar Pradesh, India, busted a langur smuggling operation, arresting one suspect and recovering ten langurs, a leaf-eating monkey species, that had been illegally trafficked out of forest land in neighboring Pilibhit district. Translated from Hindi-language reporting.

title: Barbary Macaque Escapes Zoo in Ueckermunde, Germany, Bound for Tenerife
summary: A male Barbary macaque due to be transferred from a zoo in Ueckermunde to a monkey park in Tenerife escaped its quarantine enclosure and was spotted on public streets near the zoo. It evaded capture, climbed trees, and returned to zoo grounds on its own overnight, though it took further effort, including a standoff in a greenhouse, to fully recapture it. No injuries were reported. Translated from German-language reporting.

title: Capuchin Monkey Bites Man Near Reservoir in Catalao, Brazil
summary: A 37-year-old man was bitten on the foot by a capuchin monkey while walking near a reservoir in Catalao, Goias, Brazil, as his wife filmed a small group of monkeys nearby. He did not notice the wound immediately because he was wearing shoes, then sought treatment and received a rabies vaccine dose at a local emergency clinic. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting.

title: Elderly Woman Dies After Monkey Attack in Palwal, India
summary: A 75-year-old woman was bitten by a monkey while sitting in her courtyard in Pingwan village, Palwal district, Haryana, India. She was initially treated with rabies injections at a local government hospital but later died during continued treatment at Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Five Smuggled Spider Monkeys Seized at US-Mexico Border Near Brownsville
summary: Agents near Brownsville, Texas, apprehended a person who had crossed the border illegally carrying a backpack containing five Mexican spider monkeys -- three infants and two juveniles -- along with a kinkajou. The primates were turned over to Gladys Porter Zoo, which says it has now taken in roughly 19 baby spider monkeys seized from smugglers across South Texas border crossings so far this year.

title: Wild Monkeys Captured After Repeatedly Entering Residential Area in Dong Nai, Vietnam
summary: A forestry response team captured three wild monkeys that had repeatedly entered a residential area of Bien Hoa, Dong Nai province, Vietnam, attacking pet dogs and cats and damaging property; officials said the animals posed a risk to residents, especially children, though no human injuries were confirmed. The monkeys were relocated to the Dong Nai Nature and Cultural Reserve. Translated from Vietnamese-language state media reporting.

title: Man Suffers Multiple Fractures Falling From Roof While Fleeing Monkey Troop in Agra, India
summary: A young man fell from a rooftop in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India, while trying to escape a troop of monkeys, sustaining fractures to both legs, his spine, and his hip. Troop size was not specified in the source and is an approximate estimate here. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Loose Pet Lemur Captured by Police in Belton, Texas
summary: A pet lemur got loose in Belton, Texas, prompting a call to police, who described the animal as fast, furry, and reluctant to cooperate. Officers detained the lemur and returned it to its owner; the exact lemur species was not specified in initial coverage.

title: Wild Macaques Repeatedly Enter Residential Buildings in Sha Tin, Hong Kong
summary: A troop of about five wild rhesus macaques climbed onto the podium of a residential building near Sha Tin, Hong Kong on August 4, then breached the same building again around August 14 -- the third such incursion at the estate in 2026, after roughly a dozen monkeys sheltered there during a typhoon in late July. A separate macaque was spotted outside a unit at the nearby Yue Tin Court estate on September 2, prompting AFCD to set capture cages and management to warn residents to keep windows shut. A local district councillor raised concerns that Yu Lan Festival food offerings could be drawing the established hillside macaque population further into the city; Hong Kong's agriculture department (AFCD) said it has logged nearly 1,500 monkey-nuisance reports over the past five years and has increased patrols. Translated from Chinese-language reporting.

title: Japanese Macaque "Luka" Escapes Highland Wildlife Park in Scotland
summary: Luka, a young male Japanese macaque, escaped his enclosure overnight at Highland Wildlife Park in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park. The Royal Zoological Society of Scotland used drones with thermal cameras to search the surrounding area and asked the public to keep their distance, saying he posed no danger. Luka returned to his enclosure on his own the following evening and was given a veterinary check before rejoining his troop; staff said such escapes can follow a male being pushed out of the group's social hierarchy.

title: Girl Injured in Monkey Attack in Shravasti, India
summary: A young girl was bitten and injured by a monkey in Bhinga, Shravasti district, Uttar Pradesh, India, part of a wider wave of monkey-attack reports across several Uttar Pradesh districts in mid-August 2026. On August 24, a boy was also injured in a separate monkey attack in the same district. Details on the animals' fate were not specified in initial reporting. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Illegal Sale of Five Ring-Tailed Lemurs Busted in New Taipei, Taiwan
summary: New Taipei City's Animal Protection Office and police intercepted an illegal sale of five ring-tailed lemurs -- a lemur species native to Madagascar, not a monkey -- found caged in a vendor's van in a temple parking lot in Zhonghe District. The suspected seller faces referral to prosecutors under Taiwan's Wildlife Conservation Act, with penalties up to five years in prison and a roughly US$47,000 fine; the lemurs were transferred to Taipei Zoo for care. Translated from Chinese-language reporting.

title: Capuchin Monkey Captured After Roaming Residential Neighborhood in Teresina, Brazil
summary: A capuchin monkey that had been circulating through the Promorar neighborhood of Teresina, Piaui, Brazil for several days, entering homes, was captured unharmed by the city's Municipal Civil Guard environmental protection unit and sent to a federal wildlife triage center for evaluation. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting.

title: Orangutan "Didi" Escapes Solo Safari Zoo Enclosure in Indonesia
summary: Didi, a male orangutan at Solo Safari zoo in Surakarta, Central Java, pulled loose an electric deterrent cable and defeated all four layers of his enclosure's containment. He wandered into a nearby neighborhood near Universitas Sebelas Maret, entering a food stall and knocking over parked motorcycles, before zoo staff tranquilized and recovered him roughly 40 minutes later. No injuries were reported and zoo management publicly apologized, announcing a security review of the enclosure. Translated from Indonesian-language reporting.

title: Monkey Troop Injures More Than a Dozen Residents Over Three Weeks in Moradabad, India
summary: A monkey troop repeatedly attacked residents of the Mora Ki Milak area of Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, India, and neighboring localities over roughly a month, injuring at least 16 people -- including a child who suffered a fractured hand and another bitten on the heel -- by mid-August. District Magistrate Rajendra Painsiya formed a special task force with anti-rabies vaccine response, and a rescue operation trapped 96 monkeys across the area for relocation, but a man was still bitten on both hands on August 17, and by August 30 more than two dozen residents had been injured within a single week in the neighboring Pakbara police station area, with residents reportedly unable to sit in courtyards or eat outdoors -- indicating the problem was not resolved despite the ongoing task-force response. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; exact species not specified in coverage.

title: Recurring Monkey Attacks Spread Across Shrinagar, Uttarakhand, India
summary: A troop of monkeys repeatedly attacked pilgrims, temple staff, and residents at the Maa Dhari Devi Temple in Shrinagar, Pauri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand, India, through August 2026, injuring at least four people over one four-day span in mid-August alone, including a child, a visiting girl, and temple workers, and snatching belongings from devotees. By early September the menace had spread beyond the temple to residential lanes across the city -- including Gurudwara Road, Nageshwar Lane, Kamleshwar, Nursery Road, Banswada, and areas near the GIC/GGIC schools -- with monkeys damaging rooftop plants, opening water tank lids, and stealing food from homes. Troop size is an approximate estimate. The temple committee asked the forest department to install capture cages on the premises. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Pet Marmoset Found Loose on Porch in Southeast Shelby County, Tennessee
summary: Shelby County sheriff's deputies responded to a home in southeast Shelby County, Tennessee, and found a pet marmoset loose on the front porch. The small monkey was taken to a veterinarian for a checkup and was reunited with its owner on August 22.

title: USDA Warns Massachusetts Lab Biomere Over Repeat Primate Handling Violations
summary: USDA issued an official warning letter to Biomere (Biomedical Research Models / JOINN Biomere), a contract-research lab in Worcester, Massachusetts, citing critical and repeat Animal Welfare Act violations in its handling of research primates. Inspectors documented a November 2025 incident in which a technician mishandled an anesthesia machine during surgery prep, trapping gas under a monkey's skin; the animal was later euthanized. Inspectors also found six separate cases of primates biting and wounding each other's fingers through inadequate caging, requiring finger amputations, plus a case where post-surgical pain medication was not administered. No escape occurred; animals remained contained at the facility.

title: Seven Primates, Including Langurs, Escape Enclosure at Vietnam Tourism Site
summary: Vietnam's forest protection authorities ordered an urgent search after seven primates -- two northern pig-tailed macaques, three stump-tailed macaques ('red-faced monkeys'), and two silvered langurs -- escaped a wildlife-keeping enclosure at the Dray Sap-Gia Long tourism site in Dak Nong province. All seven are listed as endangered or precious/rare wildlife under Vietnamese law. Authorities ordered the operating company to reinforce its enclosures to prevent further escapes while the search continues. Translated from Vietnamese-language reporting.
sourceName: Bao Nong nghiep va Moi truong (nongnghiephuuco.vn)

title: Monkey Skull Found in Passenger's Hand Luggage at Delhi Airport
summary: CISF security screening at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport discovered what appeared to be a monkey skull, along with an unusual silver-inlaid wooden stick, in a passenger's hand baggage; the traveler was headed to Hyderabad. CISF handed the passenger over to police for investigation under wildlife-protection law provisions covering possession of animal remains. Translated from Hindi-language reporting.

title: Four Arrested in Libreville Over Illegal Baby Chimpanzee Trafficking
summary: Gabon's Water and Forests administration and judicial police, backed by the NGO Conservation Justice, arrested four people found in possession of a roughly nine-month-old baby chimpanzee -- a fully protected great ape species in Gabon -- that they were attempting to sell illegally in Libreville. Investigators believe the chimpanzee had previously changed hands for 350,000 CFA francs; the animal was transferred to Lekedi Park and the suspects face prison time and fines under Gabonese wildlife law. Translated from French-language reporting.

title: Langur Bites Same Man Twice Within a Week in Lakhimpur Kheri, India
summary: A langur -- a leaf-eating monkey species distinct from the region's more common rhesus macaques -- bit a 25-year-old man on the head while he rode a motorbike near Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, India, then bit him again near the eye a week later as he fled into a sugarcane field, requiring stitches. The Forest Department subsequently caught the langur, which had been causing disturbances in the district for three days, on August 26. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Wildlife Trafficking Ring Busted in Phu Tho, Vietnam, Nets Two Primates
summary: Police in Phu Tho province, Vietnam, announced the arrest of eight suspects across six separate cases for illegally trading endangered wildlife, seizing two primates (species unspecified in reporting) along with king cobras and gaur parts. The animals were turned over to forest-protection authorities. Translated from Vietnamese-language reporting.

title: Solitary Macaque Repeatedly Sighted Roaming Kobe and Akashi, Japan
summary: A solitary Japanese macaque, first spotted August 7 in Kobe's Nishi ward, continued to be sighted across the city through late August, moving through Kita, Hyogo, and Nagata wards before being seen again on August 24 in the Arino-cho area of Kita ward -- unusual since Kobe is not typical macaque troop territory. A monkey believed to be the same animal was reported on September 4 in neighboring Akashi City, just west of Kobe. City authorities issued advisories asking residents not to feed, approach, or make eye contact with the animal, which remained uncaptured. Translated from Japanese-language reporting.

title: Illegal Wildlife Park Raided in Jaen, Peru, Capuchin Monkey Among Animals Rescued
summary: Peru's forestry and wildlife service Serfor, the environmental prosecutor's office, and National Police raided an unauthorized recreational park called Manantial de Vida in the Shumba Alto sector of Jaen district, Cajamarca region, finding a white-fronted capuchin monkey held in filthy, unauthorized conditions alongside an ocelot, a caiman, and tortoises. The animals were confiscated for rehabilitation. Translated from Spanish-language reporting.

title: Monkey Repeatedly Sighted Loose in Tuscaloosa, Alabama Neighborhood
summary: A live monkey has been repeatedly sighted in a residential neighborhood near 41st Street and Skyland Boulevard in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, since August 25. Tuscaloosa Police and Animal Control confirmed the sightings were genuine and asked residents not to approach, feed, or chase the animal. The monkey's species and origin -- whether an escaped pet or an animal from elsewhere -- remain unknown, and it was still at large as of August 26.

title: USDA Cites UC Davis Primate Research Center Over Repeated Injuries to Monkeys
summary: The USDA issued new Animal Welfare Act citations against the California National Primate Research Center at UC Davis after documenting a series of injuries to monkeys from faulty equipment, including a shard of PVC pipe left lodged in a monkey's cheek until it eroded surrounding tissue, a finger amputated when a monkey was trapped in a broken climbing structure, a monkey that swallowed loose cage hardware, and a fight between two monkeys that required surgery after a screw fell from a cage divider. The advocacy group PETA, which publicized the citations, renewed calls for the facility's closure, citing a pattern of injuries from broken equipment.

title: Marmoset Suspected of Rabies Confronts Family in Juazeiro do Norte, Brazil
summary: A common marmoset described as agitated and irritated entered a home in the Sao Jose neighborhood of Juazeiro do Norte, Ceara, Brazil, biting at fruit and advancing toward family members and a pet dog before firefighters netted and captured it. The animal was sent to the municipal Center for Zoonoses for rabies testing after local health authorities noted seven other marmosets had already tested positive for rabies in the area this year. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Titi and Capuchin Monkeys Among Animals Seized in Montevideo Wildlife Trafficking Raids
summary: Uruguayan police, working with the Directorate Against Organized Crime and Interpol, carried out a series of raids across Montevideo tied to an illegal wildlife trade ring operating out of the Piedras Blancas fair, seizing a titi monkey and a capuchin monkey along with turtles, parakeets, and cardinals. One man with prior wildlife-trafficking convictions was arrested. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; corroborated by two independent outlets.

title: Monkey Attacks Schoolgirl on Campus in Hisar, India
summary: A monkey attacked an eighth-grade female student on a school campus in Hisar, Haryana, India. Local reporting noted the student faced difficulty accessing hospital treatment due to lacking identification and funds. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Puerto Rico Wildlife Officers Seize Pet Baby Rhesus Macaque in Canovanas
summary: Puerto Rico's Department of Natural and Environmental Resources (DRNA) seized a roughly three-month-old rhesus macaque that a resident of Canovanas was keeping illegally as a pet, the sixth such seizure in the San Juan metro area so far this year. Officials said poachers kill mother macaques from Puerto Rico's feral rhesus colonies near Sabana Seca and Toa Baja to sell infants as pets or photo props, a practice that is illegal and carries disease-exposure risk.

title: Mexico's Profepa Launches National Campaign Against Illegal Primate Trafficking
summary: Mexico's federal environmental prosecutor Profepa launched a nationwide awareness campaign, 'Los monos no son mascotas' ('Monkeys are not pets'), targeting the illegal trade in native primates including spider monkeys, howler monkeys, and black howler monkeys. The agency said it has recovered 137 primates from the black market since 2019 -- 96 spider monkeys, 24 howlers, and 17 black howlers -- and warned that keeping primates as pets is a federal crime punishable by one to nine years in prison. Translated from Spanish-language reporting.

title: Series of Monkey Attacks Injures Child, Mother and Daughter, and Elderly Man in Bulandshahr, India
summary: Bulandshahr district, Uttar Pradesh, India, saw at least three separate monkey attacks over three weeks in August 2026: a school-age child bitten while walking home on August 7, a mother and daughter seriously injured together on August 12, and a 65-year-old man attacked in front of the Kotwali police station in Shikarpur on August 27. Each was reported separately with no indication officials had yet intervened to manage the local troop. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source outlet for all three.

title: Meru County Farmers Petition Kenyan Parliament Over Vervet Monkey Crop Raids
summary: Farmers in Nyweri, Meru County, Kenya, petitioned the National Assembly over an established local vervet monkey population repeatedly raiding banana, maize, and vegetable crops, asking that the species be added to the Kenya Wildlife Service's compensation framework for wildlife damage. No human injuries were reported; troop size was not specified in the source and is estimated here. This is the first Kenyan entry in this dataset outside the earlier Gabon chimpanzee-trafficking case.

title: 21 Endangered Spider Monkeys Found in Illegal Private Zoo During Fuel-Theft Raid in Tamaulipas, Mexico
summary: A joint Mexican Navy, federal prosecutor, and public security operation targeting fuel theft ('huachicol') across five properties in Tampico and Altamira, Tamaulipas, uncovered a ranch operating as an unauthorized private zoo holding 135 exotic animals, including 21 endangered Mexican spider monkeys alongside tigers, jaguars, a liger, hyenas, lions, bison, and a camel. Mexico's environmental enforcement agency Profepa took custody of the animals for assessment. Translated from Spanish-language reporting, corroborated by multiple independent Mexican outlets.

title: Woman Dies After Monkey Bite in Budaun, India
summary: A woman died after being bitten by a monkey in Budaun district, Uttar Pradesh, India, sparking panic in her village, according to local reporting. The exact circumstances of the bite and the animal's fate were not specified in initial coverage. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: DRNA Seizes Two Rhesus Monkeys From Barrio Obrero Residence in San Juan
summary: Puerto Rico's Department of Natural and Environmental Resources (DRNA) executed a search warrant at a residence in the Barrio Obrero sector of San Juan after a citizen tip prompted by a lieutenant's televised appeal for reports of illegally kept exotic animals. Vigilance Corps officers found two rhesus macaques in the yard and transferred them to the Exotic Species Confinement Center in Cambalache, Arecibo. This is a separate seizure from the Canovanas rhesus macaque case reported the same week.

title: Man Arrested Selling Dead Pygmy Loris in Hai Phong, Vietnam
summary: Police on patrol in Hai Phong, Vietnam, caught a young man, Tran Quoc Bao, carrying a dead pygmy loris -- a critically endangered prosimian and one of the world's smallest primate species -- that he intended to sell illegally for about 400 grams of weight. The animal was seized as evidence and police said in mid-August they were preparing charges under Vietnam's law protecting endangered species. Translated from Vietnamese-language reporting; corroborated by multiple independent outlets.

title: Langur Enters Shop, Attacks Young Man in Bahraich, India
summary: A langur -- a leaf-eating monkey species distinct from the region's more common rhesus macaques -- entered a shop in Bahraich district, Uttar Pradesh, India, and attacked a young man inside, part of a wider pattern of langur and monkey attacks reported across the district through August 2026, including separate langur bites to villagers in late July and early August. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Woman Injured in Monkey Attack in Nahan, Himachal Pradesh, India
summary: A woman was injured by monkeys at Rani Ka Bagh in Nahan town, Sirmour district, Himachal Pradesh, India. This is the first Himachal Pradesh entry in this tracker; a companion explainer piece the same day noted the state's monkey population has fallen by more than half in recent years yet attacks persist. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Elderly Woman Critically Injured Falling From Roof While Fleeing Monkey Attack in Sambhal, India
summary: An elderly woman was critically injured after falling from her rooftop while trying to escape a monkey attack in Sambhal district, Uttar Pradesh, India. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Child Hospitalized After Monkey Bite in Palwal, India
summary: A child was hospitalized after being bitten by a monkey in Palwal district, Haryana, India, a separate incident from the earlier fatal monkey-bite case reported in the same district in August 2026. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Villager Injured Falling From Roof While Fleeing Monkey Attack in Meerut, India
summary: A villager in Uldhan, Meerut district, Uttar Pradesh, India, fell from a roof and was injured while trying to escape a monkey attack. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Amroha Shopkeepers Place Langur Cutouts to Deter Marauding Monkey Troops
summary: Shopkeepers in Amroha, Uttar Pradesh, India, began placing cardboard cutouts of langurs and dogs outside their shops to scare off marauding monkey troops that have been biting people and raiding shops; earlier August reporting cited more than 4,400 monkey-bite cases treated in the district over the preceding two months. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Roaming Monkey Troops Disrupt Streets in Rohtak, India
summary: Residents of Rohtak, Haryana, India, reported that roaming monkey troops have made it difficult to walk through city streets and lanes, part of a wider pattern of monkey-menace complaints across northern India in August 2026. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Resident Files Complaint Over Worsening Monkey Menace in Chomu, Rajasthan, India
summary: A resident of Ashok Vihar Colony in Chomu, Jaipur district, Rajasthan, India, filed a formal complaint via the state's Sampark administrative portal about a worsening monkey menace in the neighborhood; the resident alleged the portal marked the complaint 'resolved' without any actual action being taken. This is the first Rajasthan entry logged in this tracker. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Wild Macaques Injure Tourist at Mount Emei Scenic Area, China
summary: A female tourist visiting the Leidongping area of Mount Emei in Sichuan, China, was attacked without provocation by two wild macaques, sustaining multiple lacerations and bruising to her legs and arms that required wound cleaning, sutures, rabies immunoglobulin, and vaccination. The Mount Emei Forestry Bureau confirmed the case, said it would increase patrols, and offered to reimburse medical costs. Exact incident date is approximate based on available reporting; translated from Chinese-language reporting, corroborated by multiple outlets.

title: Two Residents Bitten by Monkeys Over Four Days in Bijhri, Himachal Pradesh, India
summary: Two residents of Bijhri village in Hamirpur district, Himachal Pradesh, India, were bitten by monkeys over a four-day span, part of a chronic rhesus macaque problem in the state's hill districts. No capture or mitigation plan has been announced. This is the first Himachal Pradesh entry logged in this tracker. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Three Villagers Injured in Monkey Attack in Khairi Village, Budaun, India
summary: Three villagers in Khairi village near the Sahaswan/Bilsi area of Budaun district, Uttar Pradesh, India, were injured by an attacking troop of monkeys, triggering panic in the area. This is a separate incident, in a different village, from the fatal Budaun monkey-bite case reported August 28, 2026. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Fifteen People Attacked by Stray Dogs and Monkeys in a Single Day in Amroha, India
summary: Fifteen people across several villages in Amroha district's Jyotiba Phule Nagar area, Uttar Pradesh, India, were bitten by stray dogs and monkeys in a single day, with the local hospital reporting 20 to 25 bite victims a day seeking anti-rabies treatment. This follows an earlier Amroha report from August 29, 2026, about shopkeepers using langur cutouts to deter marauding monkey troops. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Female YouTuber Attacked by Monkey Troop in Bairampur Village, Budaun, India
summary: A YouTuber identified as Krishna Devi was attacked by a troop of monkeys in Bairampur village, Budaun district, Uttar Pradesh, India, sustaining deep lacerations to her hand that required 20 stitches at a community health center. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Wild Macaque Roams Shizuoka City Neighborhood for Four Days
summary: A lone adult male Japanese macaque was repeatedly sighted over four days in residential streets west of the Abekawa River in Suruga Ward, Shizuoka City, Japan, climbing utility poles and pushing through a resident's gate. No injuries were reported, though officials noted the prefecture has seen monkey-bite incidents before and continued monitoring the animal. Translated from Japanese-language reporting; corroborated by multiple outlets.

title: Pet Long-Tailed Macaque Turns Aggressive, Escapes in Ciamis, Indonesia
summary: A resident's pet long-tailed macaque suddenly became aggressive and broke loose, climbing a tree in Linggapura village, Kawali district, Ciamis regency, West Java, Indonesia. A local fire brigade crew captured and secured the animal within about an hour; no injuries were reported. Translated from Indonesian-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Captive Capuchin Monkey Rescued in Maracaibo, Venezuela
summary: Venezuelan environmental authorities in Zulia state rescued a young captive capuchin monkey from a home in the Los Estanques neighborhood of Maracaibo after a community tip from a local environmental group. Officials said the animal cannot be released back into the wild due to the effects of prolonged captivity. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; single-source account (republished by one additional outlet).

title: Man Arrested After Capuchin Monkey Found Caged in Calarca, Colombia
summary: Colombian National Police and the regional environmental authority CRQ raided a rural property in the Potosi district of Calarca, Quindio department, finding a capuchin monkey caged in poor conditions; a second capuchin was seen on the property's roof but evaded capture. A 53-year-old man was arrested and turned over to prosecutors. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Tourist Bitten by Monkey at the Taj Mahal, Agra, India
summary: A female tourist visiting the Taj Mahal in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India, was bitten by a monkey on the monument grounds. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Years-Long Monkey Menace Leaves Children Fearful in Ballia, India
summary: Residents of Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh, India, described a monkey menace stretching back roughly three years, with several people injured in repeated attacks and children reportedly afraid to go outside. This is the first Ballia entry logged in this tracker. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Residents Report Worsening Monkey Menace in Pakbada, Moradabad, India
summary: Residents of Pakbada, a locality in Moradabad district, Uttar Pradesh, India, reported an ongoing monkey menace causing panic in the area, a separate report from the larger Mora Ki Milak monkey-attack response covered elsewhere in this district. Troop size is an approximate estimate. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Escaped Monkeys Bite Three Residents in Salqin, Syria
summary: Three escaped monkeys bit three residents in the city of Salqin in Syria's western Idlib countryside, sending the injured to Salqin Central Hospital and prompting some bystanders to flee as videos of the animals running through the streets circulated on social media. Capture efforts were underway as of the report; it was the second such escape reported in Salqin in recent months, after a group of monkeys broke out of a local amusement park in June and roamed the Qusour neighborhood before being located.

title: Jane Goodall Institute Calls on York University to Retire Nine Research Macaques
summary: The Jane Goodall Institute issued a statement saying it was deeply troubled by the conditions of nine rhesus macaques used in neuroscience research at York University in Toronto and called on the university to immediately retire the animals to a sanctuary. The statement followed an undercover investigation released earlier in the year by Last Chance for Animals, in which an investigator worked inside the university's Behavioural Sciences Building for nine months and documented the macaques living in small cages with head-post implants and collar restraints. York University has continued to defend its primate research program despite public protests.

title: Wild Pig-Tailed Macaque Injures Resident in Vung Tau, Vietnam, Then Captured
summary: An adult wild pig-tailed macaque entered a home on Vi Ba road, near Lon Mountain in Vung Tau ward (now part of Ho Chi Minh City following Vietnam's administrative merger), and attacked a resident, who suffered a bleeding injury and significant blood loss. Local authorities captured the adult monkey the same afternoon. The area saw a similar spate of macaque attacks in late January 2026 that ended when authorities captured several aggressive monkeys. Translated from Vietnamese-language reporting; corroborated by two independent outlets.

title: Adult Spider Monkey Seized from Residence in Nueva Italia, Mexico
summary: Michoacan state prosecutors and Mexico's federal environmental protection agency Profepa raided a residence in Nueva Italia, Michoacan, and seized an adult male spider monkey that had been kept illegally as a pet. The animal was transferred to Morelia Zoo, where staff found injuries to its mouth and knees and signs of prolonged close contact with humans; it remained under veterinary observation. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; multiple outlets confirmed the seizure.

title: Forest Department Investigates Actor Over Lar Gibbons Kept at Private Farm in Tamil Nadu, India
summary: A since-deleted social media video showing Tamil actor Vikram with a young lar gibbon, a protected ape species native to Southeast Asia, prompted the Tamil Nadu Forest Department to open a trafficking investigation. Records showed three lar gibbons had been transferred without wildlife clearances to a farm in Erode in June 2026; one female gibbon died shortly after arrival without the death being reported, and the two survivors are pending confiscation. The case was reported by more than eight independent Indian outlets.

title: Two Primates Found Dead in Raid on Unlicensed Wildlife Sanctuary in Bandera County, Texas
summary: Constables and game wardens executing a search-and-seizure warrant at We Care Wildlife Sanctuary in Lakehills found more than 20 dead animals, including two primates whose species was not disclosed in initial reports, alongside roughly 15 dead horses. Over 100 surviving animals were seized amid an animal-cruelty and neglect investigation; the two dead primates were sent for forensic necropsy. The facility had prior legal disputes over ownership of a pet capuchin monkey.

title: Loose Monkey Climbs Rooftops and Power Lines in San Juan de Lurigancho, Lima, Peru
summary: Residents of the Los Alamos area in San Juan de Lurigancho, a district of Lima, reported a monkey -- described by outlets as a 'mono choro' (woolly monkey) or squirrel monkey -- moving along overhead cables and rooftops and taking fruit from homes. Security personnel attempted to reach the animal with a ladder but could not capture it, and residents asked Peru's forestry and wildlife service (SERFOR) to intervene. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; multiple Lima outlets covered the sighting.

title: Monkey Troop Attacks Rickshaw Driver Who Tried to Help Injured Baby Monkey in Bareilly, India
summary: A 45-year-old rickshaw puller named Sharafat was bitten on the heel by a troop of monkeys in the Subhashnagar police station area of Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, India, after he stopped to help an injured baby monkey lying in the road. A temple priest assisted him and he was taken to the district hospital for treatment. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Capuchin Monkey Rescued After Being Kept Chained in Home in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
summary: A joint operation by Tijuca National Park (ICMBio) and Rio de Janeiro's Environmental Police, triggered by a complaint filed through a federal reporting platform, rescued a female capuchin monkey found chained with very limited freedom of movement inside a home in the Santa Teresa neighborhood. Residents could not produce documentation proving legal origin, so authorities classified the animal as a trafficking victim as well as a case of mistreatment. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting; the monkey was sent to a wildlife institute for evaluation.

title: Chimpanzee Briefly Accesses Building Rooftop at Project Chimps Sanctuary
summary: A chimpanzee named Tory, a recent arrival still integrating into his social group, left his primary enclosure at the Project Chimps sanctuary and climbed onto the rooftop of his residential building, apparently seeking an indoor area amid social tension with his new group of eight chimps. He remained within the sanctuary's outer perimeter fencing throughout. A trained veterinary dart team sedated and returned him to his enclosure after he did not return voluntarily; he was examined afterward and reported doing well.

title: Two Baby Howler Monkeys Rescued from Illegal Sale in Santa Cruz, Bolivia
summary: Following a citizen tip, Bolivia's Special Force to Combat Environmental Crimes (Felcda) intervened in the Urubo area of Santa Cruz de la Sierra to stop the illegal sale of two baby howler monkeys, which were being offered for roughly 2,800 bolivianos. Two people were arrested in the operation. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; corroborated by two independent outlets.

title: Wild Monkey Filmed Rappelling Down Rio de Janeiro Apartment Building
summary: A monkey was filmed on a balcony of a residential building in the Taquara neighborhood of western Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Unable to find an easy way down, it grabbed two ropes left by construction workers and rappelled down the building's exterior before leaving the area unharmed. Outlets noted the increasing frequency of wild monkeys appearing in Rio's urban zones. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting; corroborated by two independent outlets.

title: Monkey Rampages Through Market, Injures Several in Gola, Jharkhand, India
summary: A monkey entered the market area near DVC Chowk in Gola, Ramgarh district, Jharkhand, India, knocking over shop goods and attacking several bystanders, injuring them and causing panic among shoppers. Forest department officials were alerted but the monkey had fled by the time they arrived; villagers are demanding action to prevent recurrence. This is the first Jharkhand entry logged in this tracker. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Wild Monkey Attacks Child Near School in Quang Ngai, Vietnam
summary: A wild monkey appeared near an elementary and junior high school in Tan Lap A hamlet, Dak Mar commune, Quang Ngai province, Vietnam, and attacked and injured a child. Village authorities alerted local forces, who cornered and captured the monkey the following day; officials urged residents not to approach, feed, or provoke wild monkeys. Translated from Vietnamese-language reporting; corroborated by two independent outlets.

title: Nigeria Customs Seizes 48 Trafficked Animals Including Gorillas, Chimpanzees, and Bush Babies
summary: Nigeria Customs Service's Kano/Jigawa Area Command intercepted a vehicle carrying 48 wild animals along the Kano-Daura road, including 15 primates -- two baby gorillas, four chimpanzees, and bush babies (galagos) -- alongside civets, caracals, crocodiles, a honey badger, and 25 birds. Three suspects were arrested and handed to the Special Wildlife Office for prosecution under the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023 and CITES; officials described it as the largest single wildlife seizure in the service's history. The animals were intercepted August 25 and the bust was publicized in a press briefing September 4. Corroborated by five independent outlets.
sourceName: World Animal News / EnviroNews Nigeria / Leadership.ng

title: Pet Capuchin Monkey and Baby Escape Enclosure in Fuchtorf, Germany
summary: A privately-kept mother capuchin monkey and her baby escaped their enclosure in Fuchtorf, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, after the owner stumbled while entering, startling the mother, who fled through the open door with her infant clinging to her. As of early September the pair had not been found; the owner believes they may be hiding in sheds, garages, or attics and asked the public not to attempt capture but to block escape routes and notify him. Exact escape date is approximate (reported as "the previous week"). Translated from German-language reporting; single-outlet account.

title: Five Baby Orangutans Found Abandoned in Odisha, Suspected Wildlife Smuggling Transit
summary: Villagers in the Bhograi area of Balasore district, Odisha, India, spotted five juvenile orangutans -- three males and two females, all under a year old -- in a casuarina plantation near the Udayapur-Talsari border, initially mistaking them for monkeys. Orangutans are not native to India, so forest officials suspect the animals were abandoned mid-transit by an international wildlife-smuggling operation using Odisha as a transit route. All five were moved to Nandankanan Zoological Park for quarantine; by September 11-12, Odisha's Special Task Force had questioned three suspects in West Bengal and was tracing a black SUV believed to have transported the animals, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi ordered a full probe, and Indonesia's forestry ministry said it suspects Sumatran origin and is seeking repatriation pending DNA testing.

title: Troop of Wild Macaques Repeatedly Sighted in Hamamatsu Shopping District, Japan
summary: A troop of wild Japanese macaques, numbering up to about ten at peak sightings, has repeatedly appeared around the Clover-dori shopping street and the Futamata bridge area of Tenryu Ward, Hamamatsu, Japan, with seven separate sighting reports between September 1 and September 9, 2026. The monkeys have moved across rooftops and damaged garden persimmons, though no injuries have been reported; the city issued advisories asking residents not to approach, provoke, or feed them. Translated from Japanese-language reporting.

title: Peru's SERFOR Reports 69 Monkeys Rescued From Lima Homes as Illegal Pets This Year
summary: Peru's national forestry and wildlife service SERFOR announced it has rescued 69 monkeys -- mostly monk/fraile monkeys along with capuchin, tamarin, and woolly monkeys -- kept illegally as pets in Lima households so far in 2026, most commonly in the Ate, San Juan de Lurigancho, and Comas districts, after being trafficked out of the Amazon. Officials said roughly nine monkeys die in transit for every one that survives to reach Lima, and highlighted a recent case of a six-month-old capuchin found with its tail cut and injuries from a diaper used to restrain it. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; corroborated by multiple independent outlets.

title: Langur Attacks Forest Rescue Team During Capture Attempt in Bahraich, India
summary: A gray langur that had been active in the Risia area of Bahraich district, Uttar Pradesh, India for about two weeks attacked a Forest Department team attempting to capture it near Chandrashekhar Azad Balika Inter College on September 7, injuring forest worker Asgar, who was taken to a medical college for treatment. The langur evaded capture that day but was successfully caught by the rescue team on September 10. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Yellow-Cheeked Gibbon Seized in Cross-Border Wildlife Trafficking Bust in Bangkok, Thailand
summary: A Thai man and a Cambodian man were arrested at a petrol station in Bangkok's Phaya Thai district after Thai wildlife-crime officers, working with the US Fish and Wildlife Service, posed as buyers to seize a yellow-cheeked gibbon, an endangered ape, along with a rhinoceros hornbill hidden in perforated cardboard boxes. Both suspects confessed to acting as middlemen buying wildlife in Thailand for resale to overseas buyers including in Taiwan and India, and face charges under Thailand's Wildlife Conservation and Protection Act.

title: Monkey Troop Bites Multiple Residents in Chandigarh's Sector 22, India
summary: A troop of monkeys has repeatedly bitten residents in Sector 22, Chandigarh, India, with a woman and several children among at least four people bitten as of September 10, 2026. Residents say the aggressive monkeys have made it difficult to leave their homes and are demanding municipal action. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Monkeys Attack Lawyer at Tehsil Office in Mohanlalganj, Lucknow, India
summary: Monkeys at the Mohanlalganj Tehsil complex in Lucknow, India, attacked lawyer Sonu Pal on the premises, causing minor injuries and disrupting court-related work. The incident is part of a broader pattern of monkey encounters at government office premises in the area. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Monkey Troop Attacks Woman in Rohtak, India, Referred to PGI
summary: A troop of monkeys attacked a woman in Rohtak, Haryana, India, injuring her; she was referred to Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGI) Rohtak for treatment. The incident adds to a recurring pattern of monkey encounters previously reported in the city. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Monkey Bites Assistant Superintendent of Police During Station Inspection in Baghpat, India
summary: An Assistant Superintendent of Police was bitten by a monkey while conducting an inspection at the Kotwali police station in Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh, India. The officer received treatment for the bite, and the incident underscores the frequency of monkey encounters even at government facilities in the district. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Long-Tailed Macaque Roams Residential Area for Three Days in Cipaku, Ciamis, Indonesia
summary: A long-tailed macaque was repeatedly seen roaming a residential neighborhood in Blok Tabrik, Dusun Wetan, Desa Ciakar, Cipaku district, Ciamis regency, West Java, Indonesia, over three days, at one point sleeping in a house's ceiling space. Residents grew anxious about a possible attack, and officials linked the animal's appearance to dry-season food scarcity in its natural habitat. Translated from Indonesian-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Capuchin Monkey Roams Multiple Sao Paulo Neighborhoods, Captured by Wildlife Unit
summary: A capuchin monkey ('macaco-prego') was repeatedly sighted over several days moving through multiple neighborhoods of western and central Sao Paulo, Brazil, including Bras, Lapa, Perdizes, and Agua Branca, drawing attention on social media. The Municipal Civil Guard's wildlife unit (GCM Ambiental) captured the animal on September 11, 2026, and it is being evaluated at an animal management center for possible release back into the wild. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting; single local news network's coverage.

title: Pet Capuchin Monkey Bites Child During Store Show-and-Tell in League City, Texas
summary: A pet capuchin monkey named Cody, owned by Robert Williams and kept at Ms. Monkey's Emporium on FM 2094 in League City, Texas, bit a 4-year-old boy during a show-and-tell event, breaking the skin and leaving bruising. Accounts conflict: the owner says the boy pulled the monkey's tail, while the boy's mother says the monkey jumped off the owner and ran at her son unprovoked. League City animal control suspended Williams's exhibitor license, placed Cody under a 21-day quarantine, and barred his two other monkeys from public contact pending review.
sourceName: ABC13 Houston / ABC7 Chicago / ABC11 / Click2Houston

title: Wild Macaque Sighted on Grounds of Matsue City Library, Japan
summary: A single wild Japanese macaque was spotted on the grounds of the Matsue City Library complex (Sanbiru Culture Center/Plabo Hall) in Shimane Prefecture, Japan, on the evening of September 10, 2026. The city library issued a routine public safety notice advising people not to approach, make eye contact with, or feed the animal; no injuries were reported and the monkey moved on from the area. Translated from Japanese-language reporting; single local source.

title: Macaque Bolts Into Print Shop in Changsha, China, Captured by Forestry Officials
summary: Around 1pm on September 12, 2026, a macaque ran into a print and signage shop in the Yuhua District of Changsha, Hunan, China, bolting upstairs and damaging ceiling panels but injuring no one. The shop owner trapped it on the second floor by closing the stairwell door and called the local zoo, which referred the matter to the forestry bureau; officials arrived and captured the animal. Reporters noted Changsha has no native wild macaque population, suggesting the animal was a captive or pet macaque that had escaped rather than a wild one. Translated from Chinese-language reporting (Phoenix News/ifeng.com); single source.

title: Wild Macaque Spotted Walking Power Lines in Downtown Gaoshu Township, Taiwan
summary: On the afternoon of September 13, 2026, a wild Formosan rock macaque was spotted in downtown Gaoshu Township, Pingtung County, Taiwan, near Ciyun Temple; around 5:30pm it climbed a utility pole and walked along overhead power lines, swaying acrobatically while passersby filmed it, sparking concern it could be electrocuted. Local agriculture officials noted it was the fourth reported macaque sighting in the township so far in 2026 and advised residents not to approach, startle, or feed the animal. Translated from Chinese-language reporting; corroborated by multiple Taiwanese outlets (United Daily News/udn.com and Liberty Times/ltn.com.tw).

title: Man Arrested for Trying to Sell Baby Chimpanzee in Djoum, Cameroon
summary: A 23-year-old man from Meyo III, South Region, Cameroon, was arrested on September 8, 2026, in Djoum after traveling there to find a buyer for a baby chimpanzee he had kept hidden for several weeks, having earlier shot and partly eaten the infant's mother. Forestry and wildlife agents tracked him after he failed to find a buyer locally and arrested him at the point of sale; he was held at the Djoum gendarmerie brigade, and the chimpanzee was transferred to Mefou National Park, where the NGO Ape Action Africa began providing care. Translated from French-language reporting (camer.be); single outlet.

title: Hoolock Gibbon Briefly Escapes Enclosure at Nandankanan Zoological Park, India
summary: A hoolock gibbon briefly got out of its enclosure at Nandankanan Zoological Park in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, India, on September 4, 2026, and climbed a nearby tree, alarming visitors. Before the zoo's tranquilizer team could reach it, noise from onlookers startled the gibbon and it returned to its enclosure on its own; no injuries were reported and the cause of the enclosure breach was not immediately known. Corroborated by multiple Indian outlets (OdishaTV, Pragativadi, Business News This Week).

title: Wild Macaque Bites Multiple Visitors at Qianlingshan Park, Guiyang, China
summary: A wild macaque at Qianlingshan Park in Guiyang bit a visitor surnamed Guo and a companion shortly after they entered the park, then went on to injure a male visitor as well. Guo required rabies vaccination, a tetanus shot, and immunoglobulin treatment; the park said it would only cover the cost of the rabies vaccine. The park is home to roughly 1,000 free-ranging macaques and has a history of frequent visitor injuries. Translated from Chinese-language reporting.

title: Wild Monkeys Bite Two Elderly Women in Separate Attacks in Sanyo-Onoda, Japan
summary: Two separate wild-monkey attacks struck Sanyo-Onoda City in Yamaguchi Prefecture on the same morning. A woman in her 70s was bitten on both feet and scratched on her hands near the Nagatomo intersection while taking out trash, and about 700 meters away another woman in her 70s was bitten on the buttocks while working in a rice paddy. Police believe different monkeys were involved; patrols were increased and a local elementary school asked parents to pick up children. Similar attacks occurred in the same area in May 2026. Translated from Japanese-language reporting.

title: Smuggled Long-Tailed Macaque Found Hidden in Suitcase at Juanda Airport, Indonesia
summary: Quarantine officers at Juanda International Airport in Surabaya used X-ray screening to detect a live animal hidden in a passenger's luggage, finding a long-tailed macaque concealed in a plastic-wrapped box disguised with old food packaging and bound for Bulukumba, South Sulawesi. The suspect fled and was pursued by police; the macaque was handed to the East Java Quarantine Agency for health screening, including rabies testing. Translated from Indonesian-language reporting.

title: Bonnet Macaque Escapes Enclosure at Delhi Zoo, Mauls Caretaker and Visitor
summary: A bonnet macaque got out of its enclosure at the National Zoological Park (Delhi Zoo) on Sunday night after a gate was allegedly left improperly secured, entering the staff and caretaker gallery.
