On Monday morning the monkey mauled a caretaker, severing part of a finger and biting both his legs, and also injured a visitor; the same animal reportedly attacked a different staff member in December 2025. Corroborated by multiple Indian outlets including English and Hindi-language coverage.

title: Two Chimpanzees Escape Enclosure at Taipei Zoo
summary: Two chimpanzees, a 44-year-old male named Xiaoqiang and an 11-year-old named Wawazhi, got out of their enclosure in the Africa animal area at Taipei Zoo on the afternoon of September 17. Staff evacuated and cordoned off the area, then tranquilized and recaptured both animals within about 45 minutes; no visitors or staff were injured.

title: Man Bitten by Troop of Wild Macaques in Yugawara Hot Spring District, Japan
summary: A man in his 40s was surrounded by more than a dozen wild Japanese macaques from a locally known troop while walking in front of a hot-spring inn in Yugawara, Kanagawa Prefecture, and was bitten multiple times on his hand before being taken to a hospital with minor injuries. The troop has been increasingly aggressive toward residents, and prefectural approval for a capture operation was still pending as of the report. Translated from Japanese-language reporting.

title: Troop of More Than 20 Wild Macaques Sighted Moving Through Yonago, Japan
summary: A troop of more than 20 wild Japanese macaques, believed to have migrated from neighboring Yasugi City, was repeatedly sighted moving through residential neighborhoods of Yonago, Tottori Prefecture, including on rooftops, over September 15-16. No injuries were reported; local authorities urged residents not to approach or feed the animals and to keep doors and windows locked. Translated from Japanese-language reporting.
sourceName: Nippon TV (via TVer) / Yahoo! News Japan

title: Troop of Aggressive Monkeys Attacks 16 Villagers in a Single Day in Barabanki, India
summary: A troop of aggressive rhesus macaques attacked at least 16 villagers in the Nindura-Kursi Kotwali area of Barabanki district, Uttar Pradesh, India, in a single day, causing panic; an elderly woman was seriously injured after falling while fleeing. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Monkeys Bite and Injure 12 People Over Two Days in Hisar, India
summary: Monkeys bit and injured 12 people over a two-day span in Hisar, Haryana, India, with residents reporting growing fear of the animals in residential neighborhoods. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Monkeys Terrorize Residents Across Palwal, India, Biting Several People
summary: Troops of monkeys have been moving through Palwal, Haryana, India, targeting children, the elderly, and women alone at home, with several people bitten in a recent spate of incidents. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Shimla Residents Protest After Woman Dies Following Monkey and Langur Attack
summary: Shimla's Nagrik Sabha, a citizens' body, staged a protest on September 14, 2026 demanding Rs 5 lakh in compensation for the family of a woman who died after falling from her rooftop while allegedly being attacked by monkeys and langurs as she checked a water tank in the city's Cemetery area. The protest also called for broader action against Shimla's rising monkey, langur, and stray-dog attack problem; the exact date of the fatal fall was not specified in available reporting.

title: Squirrel Monkey Rescued Wandering Between Homes in Talara, Peru
summary: Peru's forestry and wildlife service Serfor rescued a squirrel monkey found wandering between homes in the Nuevo Horizonte settlement of Talara, Piura region, after a resident reported it through the 'Alerta Serfor' citizen platform. Peru's environmental police and regional fire service assisted; officials noted the species is native to the Amazon, not the Piura coast, indicating the animal had likely been trafficked and kept illegally as a pet. It cannot be released to the wild due to its time in captivity. Translated from Spanish-language reporting.

title: Police Rescue Two Squirrel Monkeys and Two Parrots in Manta, Ecuador
summary: Ecuadorian police, responding to an ECU 911 emergency call, rescued two common squirrel monkeys and two blue-fronted parrots being illegally held in Manta, Manabi province. The animals were turned over to the Ministry of Environment for a health evaluation. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Ecuadorian Military Rescues Chained Capuchin Monkey During Home Inspection
summary: During a routine home-verification operation in Sector Primavera II, Balzar canton, Guayas province, Ecuador, Ecuadorian Armed Forces personnel found a black-faced capuchin monkey being kept illegally chained, with visible abdominal injuries. The animal was handed over to the environmental police and emergency services for veterinary care and rehabilitation. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; case was reported as under investigation with no arrest confirmed yet.

title: Macaques Bite Multiple Tourists at Huangshan Scenic Area, China
summary: Multiple tourists reported being surrounded or bitten by wild macaques at China's Huangshan (Yellow Mountain) scenic area in mid-September 2026. One woman escaped injury near West Sea Grand Canyon by throwing her hat to distract a group of two to three monkeys after photographing one; a separate female visitor suffered a 3-centimeter-deep bite wound to her thigh requiring six stitches and a course of rabies post-exposure vaccinations. The scenic area's management said it would cover medical costs and urged visitors not to feed or approach the monkeys. Translated from Chinese-language reporting.

title: Nigerian Customs Arraigns Three Over Trafficking of Baby Gorillas, Chimpanzees and Other Wildlife
summary: Nigeria Customs Service's Kano/Jigawa Area Command intercepted three men on the Kano-Daura road on August 25, 2026, with 48 live wild animals including two baby gorillas (believed to be Cross River gorillas), four chimpanzees, seven red patas monkeys, and two galagos (bush babies), along with caracals and other protected species. The suspects were formally arraigned on conspiracy and illegal wildlife trafficking charges before the Federal High Court in Kano on September 16, 2026, with the case proceeding to a bail hearing on October 7. Officials called it one of the largest single wildlife seizures in the agency's history.

title: Middle School Student Injured in Monkey Encounter Near Matsue, Japan
summary: A middle school boy sustained a minor injury after being confronted by a lone wild macaque while walking to school in Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture, Japan, on September 16, 2026. A solitary macaque was also sighted elsewhere in the city on September 9 and September 17, separate from a larger troop reported moving through nearby Yonago around the same time. Translated from Japanese-language reporting.

title: SERFOR Reports 69 Monkeys Rescued From Illegal Pet-Keeping in Lima Homes in 2026
summary: Peru's national forestry and wildlife service (SERFOR) reported that it had rescued 69 monkeys during 2026 from homes in Lima, mainly in the Ate, San Juan de Lurigancho, and Comas districts, where they were being illegally kept as pets after being trafficked out of the Amazon. The most common species involved were tufted capuchins, common squirrel monkeys, and tamarins; SERFOR said it handles roughly eight such cases per month in the capital. Translated from Spanish-language reporting.

title: Five Baby Orangutans Found Abandoned in Indian Forest, Suspected Trafficked From Indonesia
summary: Five baby orangutans, aged roughly six months to a year and a half and suspected to be Sumatran orangutans, were found abandoned in the Bichitrapur forest block of Balasore district, Odisha, India, and moved to Nandankanan Zoological Park in Bhubaneswar for quarantine and care. Since orangutans exist only in the wild in Indonesia and Malaysia, their discovery in India points to illegal cross-border trafficking, reportedly via a smuggling route through Aceh and Thailand. Indonesia's government is coordinating a repatriation effort while Odisha state authorities and India's Wildlife Crime Control Bureau investigate; custody of the animals remains unresolved.

title: Bangladesh Says Lemurs Stolen From Gazipur Safari Park Traced to India Facility; India Disputes Claim
summary: Bangladesh's Criminal Investigation Department said two of three ring-tailed lemurs stolen from Gazipur Safari Park (taken in March 2025) were smuggled into India via the Darshana border and transported to a wildlife facility in Jamnagar, Gujarat. Indian outlets disputed the claim, saying no proof has been shown that the lemurs at the Indian facility are the stolen animals. This is a contested, unresolved bilateral claim rather than a confirmed recovery.

title: Six Capuchin Monkeys Found Dead in Smuggled Baggage at Bengaluru Airport
summary: Customs officials at Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru, India, intercepted checked baggage on a flight from Bangkok, Thailand, containing 17 king cobras, 55 ball pythons, and six capuchin monkeys; all six monkeys were found dead on arrival, illustrating the high mortality common on this wildlife-smuggling route. The seizure is part of a broader pattern of exotic-animal trafficking through the Bangkok-Bengaluru corridor.

title: 40 People Injured in Monkey Attacks Over 45 Days in Nepalgunj, Nepal
summary: Nepalgunj, in Nepal's Banke District, has seen a sharp rise in wild monkey attacks, with 40 people injured over a roughly 45-day period ending around September 21, 2026, as residents try to chase monkeys off their properties. A local doctor tracking bite cases at Bheri Hospital confirmed the upward trend. dateStart is an estimate based on the reported 45-day window.

title: 91-Year-Old Woman Dies After Monkey Knocks Her Down in Koppal, Karnataka
summary: A 91-year-old woman, Najamunnisa Begum, wife of writer M.S. Savadatti, was knocked down by a monkey outside her home in B.T. Patil Nagar, Koppal district, Karnataka, India, on the evening of September 20, an incident captured on CCTV. She suffered a head injury and died in hospital the next day; the monkey reportedly also lunged at her daughter who came to help. Corrects an earlier single-source report that misattributed the incident to Bagalkot district and an earlier date.

title: Woman Dies After Falling From Roof While Fleeing Monkey Attack in Aligarh
summary: A 55-year-old woman in the Gabhana area of Aligarh district, Uttar Pradesh, India, fell to her death from a rooftop while trying to escape a monkey that roared at and charged toward her. Corroborated by multiple Hindi-language outlets. Translated from Hindi-language reporting.

title: Man Dies 15 Days After Falling From Roof While Chasing Monkeys That Took His Lunch, Agra
summary: A 50-year-old man in the Runkta area of Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India, had his lunch snatched by monkeys on September 4, 2026, and was critically injured falling from a roof while chasing them to retrieve it. He died in hospital roughly 15 days later after treatment failed. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; part of a broader pattern of monkey-related injuries and deaths reported in Agra district through 2026.

title: Cape Town Plan to Permanently Cage About 60 Chacma Baboons Sparks Outcry
summary: The City of Cape Town, South Africa, is moving forward with an Action Plan to permanently capture and cage around 60 wild chacma baboons from the Waterfall and Seaforth troops near Simon's Town into a newly completed R10 million Urban Wildlife Centre at Kogelfontein, with healthy males to be vasectomised, as an alternative to culling amid escalating human-baboon conflict. Residents and conservation groups have strongly opposed the plan, calling permanent captivity of wild baboons a dangerous precedent and pushing for coexistence measures instead. The relocation remains subject to a Wild Animal Captivity Permit.

title: Illegally Kept Spider Monkey Rescued From Home in Escobedo, Mexico
summary: A Geoffroy's spider monkey being kept illegally inside a home in the Villas del Parque neighborhood of Escobedo, Nuevo Leon, Mexico, was reported by a neighbor and captured by community police and Animal Welfare officials using a piece of banana. The animal was handed over to state authorities for a health evaluation, and the Nuevo Leon state prosecutor's office opened an investigation since possession of the protected species is illegal in Mexico. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; corroborated by multiple outlets including Milenio and Publimetro Mexico.

title: Rare Albino Wild Japanese Macaque Sighted Near Yonezawa, Japan
summary: A rare albino Japanese macaque known locally as the 'Azuma white monkey,' a designated natural monument, was spotted foraging for chestnuts with its wild troop in the Riyama forest area near Yonezawa, Yamagata Prefecture. The animal belongs to an established wild macaque population that local authorities periodically monitor. Translated from Japanese-language reporting; single source found.

title: USDA Complaint Accuses Jungle Friends Primate Sanctuary of Animal Welfare Act Violations
summary: A USDA complaint alleges Jungle Friends Primate Sanctuary, located in Alachua County near Gainesville, Florida, violated the Animal Welfare Act by failing to provide primates proper food, veterinary care, and safe living conditions, citing unsanitary and rusty enclosures. The sanctuary, home to roughly 298 rescued monkeys, was the subject of a similar USDA draft inspection report flagging deteriorating conditions in 2021. Founder Kari Bagnall disputes that important context is missing from the complaint and says corrective action has been taken.

title: Neighbors Report Capuchin Monkey Kept Illegally in Cuernavaca Apartment
summary: Residents of the La Joya housing development in Cuernavaca, Morelos, Mexico, reported the alleged presence of a capuchin monkey being kept inside a neighboring apartment, raising concerns about illegal possession of a protected wild species under Mexico's General Wildlife Law. Neighbors asked authorities to intervene and relocate the animal. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; single source, outcome not yet confirmed.

title: Wild Macaque Troop Raids Crops and Homes in Nyalian Village, Bali, Indonesia
summary: A large troop of wild long-tailed macaques believed to be moving along the Tukad Bubuh river corridor has spent roughly a month raiding farmland and increasingly entering residential areas of Nyalian village in Banjarangkan district, Klungkung regency, Bali, Indonesia, destroying coconut, durian, and other crops and causing some farmers total harvest losses. The local disaster management agency (BPBD Klungkung) said it has struggled to intervene because the animals disperse before officials arrive and the area is part of the macaques natural range, making removal difficult. No injuries to people have been reported. Translated from Indonesian-language reporting, corroborated by multiple local outlets.

title: Monkeys Bite Elderly Brazilian and Indian Tourists at the Taj Mahal, Agra
summary: Monkeys at the Taj Mahal complex in Agra, India, bit an 83-year-old Brazilian tourist and separately bit or scratched a tourist from West Bengal on the same day; both received treatment. The incident is part of a recurring pattern of monkey bites on visitors at the monument, including a separate attack on a female tourist reported there on September 3, 2026. Corroborated by multiple Indian outlets.

title: Young Man Hospitalized Falling From Retaining Wall While Fleeing Monkey Attack in Shimla, India
summary: A young man was attacked by monkeys in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, India, and fell from a retaining wall while trying to flee, sustaining injuries that required hospitalization. This follows a September 14, 2026 protest by Shimla residents over the city's worsening monkey, langur, and stray-dog menace after a woman's fatal fall during a similar attack. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-source account.

title: Spider Monkey Found Tied by the Neck to a Tree During Raid in Apatzingan, Mexico
summary: During a search warrant at a property in the Palo Alto neighborhood of Apatzingan, Michoacan, Mexico, state prosecutors, the army, National Guard, and Profepa found an approximately eight-year-old spider monkey -- an endangered species whose possession as a pet is illegal in Mexico -- tied by the neck with a plastic leash. The animal was secured and handed over to Profepa for protection. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; corroborated by at least nine independent Mexican outlets.

title: Man Caught Walking Illegal Pet Capuchin Monkey on a Leash in Cucuta, Colombia
summary: A police patrol in the Nuevo Horizonte neighborhood of Cucuta, Norte de Santander, Colombia, found a man walking a white-faced capuchin monkey tied around the waist with a chain; the animal showed signs of injury and the man could not produce ownership documentation. The species is not native to that part of Colombia, indicating illegal trafficking. The monkey was turned over to regional environmental authority CORPONOR for evaluation. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; accounts vary slightly between outlets on whether the man was arrested.

title: Wild Titi Monkey Rescued After Dog Attack in Backyard in Formiga, Brazil
summary: A black-fronted titi monkey (Callicebus nigrifrons, known locally as guigo or saua) appeared in a residential backyard in the Sao Geraldo neighborhood of Formiga, Minas Gerais, Brazil, and was attacked by the homeowner's dogs. Military firefighters captured the animal, which showed no apparent external injuries, and released it into a compatible native forest area. Translated from Portuguese-language reporting; single-outlet account.

title: Four Spider Monkeys Found Stuffed in Duffel Bag at Texas Border Checkpoint
summary: A Border Patrol K-9 alerted agents to four spider monkeys stuffed inside a duffel bag in a vehicle at the Javier Vega Jr. checkpoint near Sarita, Texas. The driver could not produce documentation or veterinary records proving lawful ownership of the endangered primates. The animals were turned over to USDA and US Fish and Wildlife Service for care.

title: Monkey Troop Attacks Student and Two Teachers at School in Amroha, India
summary: A troop of monkeys nesting on the grounds of a school in Zoya, Amroha district, Uttar Pradesh, India, attacked and injured a student and two teachers on September 16, 2026; two more teachers were separately hurt falling while fleeing the same troop. The school, with roughly 268 students, said the monkeys have become a daily disruption, following an earlier bite on a teacher and a seventh-grade student about two weeks prior. Translated from Hindi-language reporting; single-outlet account across two follow-up articles.

title: Pygmy Marmoset Surrendered as Wildlife-Trafficking Victim in Medellin, Colombia
summary: A pygmy marmoset -- the smallest neotropical monkey species, native to the western Amazon basin rather than the Medellin region -- was voluntarily surrendered to the Wildlife Care, Assessment and Rehabilitation Center run by the Valle de Aburra metropolitan environmental authority. Officials said the animal's presence far outside its natural range points to illegal wildlife trafficking, and that its high degree of habituation to humans will likely prevent it from ever being released back into the wild; the center has received only six pygmy marmosets since 2014. Translated from Spanish-language reporting; corroborated by multiple independent outlets.
